extracted.intended_audience: scholarly publishers, journal editors, editorial staff, and publishing professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for publishers and journal editors on improving the composition, inclusivity, and sustainability of peer review (e.g., collecting reviewer demographics, diversifying editorial boards and reviewer pools, mentoring co-reviewers, and exploring community/participant review models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer diversity (gender, geography, career stage, race/ethnicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase representation of women, early career, international scientists, and racially/ethnically diverse individuals in the invited reviewer pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer pool should align more closely with the demographic distribution of authors of accepted papers and with AGU member demographics. Examples: increase editors and reviewers from China, India, Mexico, Central and South America; increase proportion of women editorial board members (AGU increased ~20% since 2012). Diversifying viewpoints and lived experiences is important for what gets published and the scientific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce reviewer fatigue and expand reviewer pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to reducing reviewer fatigue while expanding and diversifying the pool of volunteer referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps include programs to mentor new reviewers and lower barriers to participation. AGU launched a Co-Reviewer pilot to offer guidance and mentorship to early career researchers and new contributors, helping attract qualified referees who might otherwise be unsure how to get involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic data collection and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and merge editorial operational data with member profile data to establish baselines and monitor reviewer demographics (country, gender, age, race/ethnicity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author and reviewer country comes from submission system profiles (97% country coverage in 2020). Gender from member database; when missing, a third-party gender API is used (returns binary gender by first name and country), and AGU's profile allowed 'non-binary' starting 2020. Race/ethnicity and age come from member profiles but reporting is often low for non-U.S. members (22% of all invited reviewers had race/ethnicity data in 2020; 49% for U.S.-based reviewers). Use these data to draw statistically significant conclusions and set goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align reviewer pool with authorship demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for the reviewer pool to mirror the demographic distribution of authors of accepted papers and the broader membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorship has higher proportions of non-Western scientists than reviewers, chief editors should be given targets to close gaps. Presenting data that highlights mismatches (e.g., many authors from China vs few editors/associate editors from China) exposes clear gaps editors can work to close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve demographic taxonomy and avoid misclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: Broaden demographic taxonomy beyond U.S. census categories to accurately capture international and complex identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize complexities (e.g., a Senegalese researcher based in the UK studying in Boston being miscategorized as 'African American'). AGU worked with its Diversity and Inclusion Advisory Committee to broaden taxonomy so fewer people are relegated to 'other'. Better taxonomy improves data quality and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board diversity as a lever for reviewer diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use editorial board composition (editors and associate editors) to influence and expand the reviewer pool's diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief editors and editorial boards invite reviewers; increasing diversity among editors (gender, geography, race/ethnicity) can produce ripples across reviewer recruitment. AGU increased percentage of women editorial board members and expanded geographical representation, which helps diversify reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use operational metrics to set diversity goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use metrics and data analysis to reveal gaps and set clear targets for editorial leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merging editorial and membership data reveals targets for chief editors (e.g., identifying underrepresentation of editors from specific countries relative to authorship). Metrics help quantify progress and inform invitation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/community review inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimagine peer review models to include community-led or participant review processes, particularly for community-focused research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU's Community Science initiative envisions a platform where community members are involved at all stages, with a participant review process ensuring usefulness of articles, reports and resources. This extends peer review beyond academia and invites community leaders to judge usefulness and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide funding/incentives for community/non-traditional reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that community reviewers and some non-academic editors lack traditional academic incentives and may need financial or other support to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recruit and sustain participation from community leaders and other non-traditional reviewers, journals/societies should seek funding or other incentives to compensate their time, since these participants may not receive academic credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with coalitions and adopt shared standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with external organizations and multi-publisher coalitions to create standards, best practices, and pooled demographic data for inclusion/diversity efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU cites learning from C4DISC, antiracism toolkits, and the Joint Commitment for Action on Inclusion and Diversity in Publishing. Pooling data across members helps produce a more complete picture and common goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewer mentorship programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement mentorship/co-reviewer programs to guide early career researchers and new contributors in how to participate in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such pilots provide guidance and mentorship, lower barriers to entry, and attract qualified referees who might otherwise be unsure how to get involved. They also serve to expand and diversify reviewer pools while building reviewer capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor participation trends and transparently report progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and publicly report longitudinal metrics on reviewer and author participation (numbers and proportions by gender, geography, race, career stage) over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU used figures showing volunteers from 2017–2020, percentage of volunteers identifying as 'woman', geographical growth of editorial board representation, and maps of editors' countries to demonstrate progress. Transparent reporting helps assess impact and guide next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and communicate reviewing as career-positive activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Address perceptions that reviewing is 'thankless' by promoting the professional benefits of reviewing, especially for early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight benefits such as increased visibility, opportunities for editorial roles, exposure to emerging research, and improved writing/editing skills to encourage participation among early career researchers who may fear time costs relative to tenure activities.
